title: Getting mad at the smoke alarm
author: The Work Forward
summary: Burnout in the American workforce is surging, with 67% of employers reporting increased mental-health-related leaves, and yet many companies respond with irritation at the requests rather than addressing the underlying causes. AI has paradoxically increased workload expectations rather than reducing them, with tech worker burnout jumping eleven points in a single year. The phenomenon of 'AI brain fry' — cognitive fatigue from overseeing AI systems — adds another layer of mental exhaustion. The article argues that leaders who respond to burnout by trying to limit leave requests are 'getting mad at the smoke alarm' rather than addressing the fire. Recovery must be reframed as a cognitive intervention, not a wellness indulgence. Boundaries and white space in calendars are leadership and team-norm issues, not personal wellness choices.
points: 67% of US employers report a rise in mental-health-related leaves, yet many respond by trying to limit requests rather than fix underlying causes.
AI has increased rather than decreased workload pressure — burnout among tech workers jumped from 45% to 56% in a single year.
'AI brain fry' — cognitive fatigue from overseeing AI systems — produces more critical errors, decision fatigue, and higher intent to quit.
Every workweek with no recovery built into it accumulates 'boundary debt'; rising mental health leave is the balance coming due.
Physical recovery should be reframed as a cognitive intervention — knowledge workers are information athletes who need recovery to perform.
quotes: We used to talk about flourishing. Now, we're just trying to prevent people from breaking down so badly that their health forces them to quit.
Spring Health says one in three of its inbound client conversations is now about how to limit leave requests. They're getting mad at the smoke alarm.
AI makes starting any task frictionless, so people fill the old gaps with another burst of output.
Every workweek with no recovery built into it runs up a kind of boundary debt. Rising mental health leave is the balance coming due.
A meditation app doesn't fix a calendar with no white space in it. Boundaries do, and boundaries don't set themselves.
